gaps.quote: Guards are equidistributed at every spectator choice
gaps.note: The page never says what a spectator choice is (the remaining address coordinates) nor why each guard is equidistributed: this holds because the y and z chunks range over all their values at every fixed choice of the other coordinates. The count of exceptional addresses rests on this and the reader cannot check it from the page.

gaps.quote: $S_0$ has at most eight rotations and sixteen swaps (cited).
gaps.note: The page never says why a rotation needs swaps. In the paper (line 2117) the target chunk is moved to the rightmost of the three chunk positions by a swap and the swap is undone after the rotation, giving two swaps per rotation and so sixteen. The page states only the count, with no role or reason, and the count stands in for how the construction works.

gaps.quote: its rank (current rank plus signed chunk differences times strides) is the key, and its hole is marked
gaps.note: Record rank, strides and marking a hole are never defined, and the page does not say how reversing the eight additions gives the destination or why the rank formula holds. The reader cannot check that the keys equal the holes' ranks or that sorting and refilling apply T_0.

gaps.quote: Schoolbook arithmetic on counters costs $O(A_{\rm rect}^3)$ per record
gaps.note: The page never says which counters or which arithmetic is performed (a record-rank counter, division into mixed-radix field values, reversing eight modular additions over up to f selected positions with f at most A_rect). Schoolbook operations on A-bit integers cost O(A^2), so the reader cannot see why the exponent is three.
